findings.title: Section-to-detail replacement invalidates an outgoing Shelf source and blocks navigation
findings.sharedOwner: DetailPanel resolved render identity/payload, typed Shelf source lifetime and detail-section host publication
consumers: All shallow detail and section transitions
findings.state: Actual signed-in normal-development failure reproduced twice, including after hard reload; source and compiler contract confirmed; fix not applied
findings.confidence: High for observed failure and source contract breach; intermediate live reactive reads not instrumented
findings.rootCause: Outgoing keyed RowDetails props remain live getters over a newly shaped shared detail union. Its href and derived source disappear before every outgoing consumer is disposed; the once-created Shelf adapter still dereferences its asserted non-null source.
findings.smallestOption: Publish a coherent per-identity resolved render snapshot in the existing detail owner; keep outgoing component props and section presentation bound to it until disposal, with a separate pending target and existing freshness/access controls.
alternatives: Where source replacement is intentional, enforce fixed source-family/identity ownership at the sourced-Shelf component boundary and dispose/recreate coherently without resetting equivalent same-owner state.
rejectedPartialRepairs: Defaulting to an unrelated medium configuration
Catching the render exception without restoring ownership
acceptance: Repeat actual 50-link Library Listen section to real music detail with zero uncaught errors and correct body
Back/Forward/close/reopen preserves filters/page/scroll/history and expected detail
Actual section/item transitions across every enabled medium and all source families; record absent real families as gaps
Pending response/import replacement and teardown never expose undefined/wrong-family configuration to outgoing adapters; late reads cannot publish
Immediate account/feature withdrawal preserves privacy; coherent snapshots do not extend authorization
Personal/party playback, reader visibility, editions, focus and overlay controls remain correct
